name: 84 Harcourt Street — early-Victorian townhouse with surviving cast-iron entrance fittings
historical_description: Terraced two-bay, four-storey former townhouse over basement, built circa 1830 and now in use as a hotel. The National Inventory of Architectural Heritage describes red brick walls laid in Flemish bond, channelled granite walling at ground-floor level, a round-headed doorway with cast-iron Scamozzian Ionic columns, panelled frieze and cornice, and a studded timber panelled door. The shared granite entrance platform has a cast-iron bootscraper and nosed granite steps. Cast-iron railings topped with anthemion finials stand over a carved granite plinth enclosing the basement well. A cast-iron coal-hole cover is recorded in the street to the west.
historical_significance: The NIAH appraisal identifies this townhouse as part of a unified terrace of Nos. 83–86 Harcourt Street and highlights its surviving Scamozzian Ionic doorcase, balconettes and decorative cast-iron railings. Its entrance and pavement fittings preserve evidence of historic domestic servicing and street-level craftsmanship.
